title: Rank-one Thom isomorphism
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a
vector bundle of constant
rank one, with the zero section $z:B\hookrightarrow E$. The zero
section is an effective Cartier divisor of $E$ (the zero scheme of the
tautological section of $\pi^*E$); let

$$
\operatorname{thom}(E):z_*\Lambda_B\longrightarrow\Lambda_E(1)[2]
$$

be its class $\operatorname{cl}_{z(B)}$ of [lem-pur-divisor-class],
and put

$$
\tau_E:=
R\pi_!\operatorname{thom}(E):
\Lambda_B\longrightarrow R\pi_!\Lambda_E(1)[2].
$$

Then $\tau_E$ is an isomorphism, compatible with base change. Its
inverse $\operatorname{tr}_\pi$ is the *rank-one vector-bundle
trace*. In particular

$$
R\pi_!\Lambda_E\;\cong\;\Lambda_B(-1)[-2].
$$

proof.text: Work at the finite level $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, for the arbitrary $n\geq1$ of [def-pur-conventions]. By [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section], locally on $B$ the pair $(E,z)$ is $(\operatorname{Spec}R[t],V(t))$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective in $R[t]$ for every $R$, including nonreduced $R$, by comparing coefficients. Thus $z(B)$ is Cartier [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], and remains Cartier after every change of base. The same local polynomial presentation makes $\pi$ separated and of finite type (its relative diagonal has ideal $(t_1-t_2)$); it is smooth of relative dimension one by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], while $z(B)\to B$ is the identity and the relative codimension is one. Hence [lem-pur-divisor-class] applies. It supplies $\operatorname{cl}(z(B))\in H^2_{z(B)}(E,A(1))$: the relative-torsor Kummer boundary of the pair $(\mathcal O_E(z(B)),s_{z(B)}|_{E-z(B)})$ at the exponent $m=\ell^n$, followed by the coefficient map of [def-pur-frame-class], namely the inverse-limit projection $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)/m\cong\mu_m$ tensored with $A$. The statement of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] says that $c_{z(B),A}$ is the pro-etale realization of the same supported morphism on its etale witness $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A$, followed by the projection-induced identification with $A_E(1)$; that ordinary etale morphism is the one of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], which by its statement is determined by the supported Kummer boundary of the same pair $(\mathcal O_E(z(B)),s_{z(B)})$ and is the scalar extension of $c_{z(B),\mathbf Z/N}$. Taking $r=n$, $N=\ell^n$, both constructions start from one relative Kummer class and apply the same projection to the twist, so under the supported-class/morphism identification of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] the class of [lem-pur-divisor-class] is the morphism $c_{z(B),A}$. Use this morphism as $\operatorname{thom}(E)$. Its local class is $\partial\kappa(t)$, so this retains the sign and normalization specified in the item.

source.place: Step 1: global class and its local equation

proof.text: The closed immersion $z$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Its compact-support functor is therefore $Rz_*=z_*$, using the compactification with identity open part in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]; exactness of closed direct image is also part of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement]. Since $\pi z=\mathrm{id}_B$, the identity-normalized composition comparison [thm-sf-comp-composition] identifies $R\pi_!z_*A_B$ with $A_B$. This is the source identification in $\tau_E=R\pi_!c_{z(B),A}$. All these maps have bounded-below etale representatives: [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] gives the representative of the supported class and of the specified finite twist, and [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies the compact direct images of these representatives with their pro-etale realizations, naturally on morphisms. In particular $\tau_E$ is the realization of an actual etale morphism, not just a map between objects separately known to come from that site.

source.place: Step 1: definition and source of the induced global morphism

proof.text:
Let $g:B'\to B$ be arbitrary, and write $v:E'=E\times_BB'\to E$, $\pi':E'\to B'$ and $z':B'\to E'$. Step 1 shows that the pulled-back divisor is Cartier. Thus [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identifies $v^{-1}c_{z(B),A}$ with $c_{z'(B'),A}$, including the supported-constant and twist comparisons. Let $C_{\pi,g}:g^{-1}R\pi_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi'_!v^{-1}$ be [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Naturality applied to the supported morphism gives a commutative square between its compact direct images. Its source component is the identity of $A_{B'}$: on etale witnesses, vertical pasting and identity normalization in [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], applied to $\pi z=\mathrm{id}$, identify that component with the exchange for the identity morphism. This is also the transported pro-etale normalization in [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Consequently, under the indicated identifications,
$$C_{\pi,g}(A_E(1)[2])\circ g^{-1}(\tau_E)=\tau_{E'}.$$
This proves compatibility for the specified exchange map, including nonflat changes of base. It uses no purity exchange for $Rz^!$.

source.place: Step 3: base change, with the exchange square and its source normalization written out

proof.text: Choose a geometric point $\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$. A fibre of a line bundle is a one-dimensional vector space, so a choice of nonzero basis identifies $(E_{\bar b},z_{\bar b})$ with $(X,0)$, $X=\mathbf A^1_\Omega$. The finite twist is locally free of rank one and has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: on the etale representative this is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identifies that representative with the prescribed pro-etale twist. Thus [lem-pur-cfiber-stalk] applies to $A_E(1)[2]$. Together with the morphism identity of Step 3, it identifies the stalk of $\tau_E$ with the compact direct image of the supported class of $0\subset X$. We compute that morphism on the ordinary etale site. By [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison], applied over the field $\Omega$, this computation realizes to the desired pro-etale compact direct image. The class and twist comparison is the one in [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]; no coefficient category is silently changed.

Put $P=\mathbf P^1_\Omega$, $j:X\hookrightarrow P$, $q:P\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and let $i_\infty$ be the section at infinity. Choose an exponent $N=\ell^r$ killing $A$; it is invertible in $\Omega$. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is Noetherian, so the decomposition clause of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] gives
$$b:A(1)[2]\oplus A\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(P,A(1)[2]),$$
with second component $h=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$. Here the constant objects on the point are identified with the modules by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology]. Apply $Rq_*$ to the open--closed triangle [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] for $A_P(1)[2]$, using [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] and the compactification formula [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. This gives
$$C:=R\Gamma_c(X,A(1)[2])\xrightarrow{a}R\Gamma(P,A(1)[2])\longrightarrow A(1)[2]\longrightarrow C[1].$$
Under $b$, the middle arrow is $(1,0)$: restriction of the unit is the identity, and restriction of $h$ is zero since $\mathcal O_P(1)|_\infty$ is the trivial line bundle, whose Kummer torsor class is zero. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] now identifies $H^i(C)$ via $a$ with the kernel of $H^i(A(1)[2]\oplus A)\to H^i(A(1)[2])$, namely $H^i(A)$. Thus
$$\beta=\operatorname{pr}_2b^{-1}a:C\xrightarrow{\sim}A$$
is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology].

source.place: Step 2: supply the missing compact-support computation; unit integration paragraph

proof.text:
Let $i_0:0\hookrightarrow X$ and $\bar i_0:0\hookrightarrow P$. The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $j^{-1}\bar i_{0*}A=i_{0*}A$ and $i_\infty^{-1}\bar i_{0*}A=0$: off $0$ its sections are sections on the empty scheme, hence zero. Apply [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] to $\bar i_{0*}A$. Its counit is therefore an isomorphism
$$e:j_!i_{0*}A\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar i_{0*}A.$$
For the Cartier divisor $0\subset P$, [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] gives $c_{0,P}:\bar i_{0*}A\to A_P(1)[2]$, whose restriction to $X$ is $c_{0,X}$. Naturality of the counit $\epsilon:j_!j^{-1}\to\mathrm{id}$, part of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement], gives the equality
$$\epsilon_{A_P(1)[2]}\circ j_!c_{0,X}=c_{0,P}\circ e.$$
Thus the map $a$ of Step 5 carries the compact image of the origin class to its ordinary image on $P$. This is an equality of the actual maps, not an identification of supported cohomology with compactly supported cohomology.

source.place: Step 2: compare the supported-origin morphism with its compact image

proof.text:
The line bundle of $D_0=(x_1=0)$ on $P$ is $\mathcal O_P(1)$. Explicitly, on $D(x_0)$ its local equation is $t=x_1/x_0$ and on $D(x_1)$ its ideal has generator $1$. Dualizing gives generators $e_0=1/t$, $e_1=1$ and the transition $e_0=t^{-1}e_1$, which is the $\mathcal O(1)$ convention of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] and the dual-ideal construction of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. By [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], forgetting support is the composite with $A_P\to\bar i_{0*}A$, and its image is $c_1(\mathcal O_P(D_0))=h$. On global sections that unit is the identity on $A=R\Gamma(0,A)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology]. Hence, for the fibre map $\tau_X:A\to C$ of Step 4, Step 6 gives $a\tau_X=h=b\iota_2$, so
$$\beta\tau_X=\operatorname{pr}_2b^{-1}b\iota_2=1_A.$$
Since $\beta$ is invertible, $\tau_X=\beta^{-1}$ is invertible. In particular the supported Kummer class maps to the compact generator with coefficient $+1$.

source.place: Step 2: the origin maps to the normalized compact generator; unit normalization paragraph

proof.text: Steps 4--7 show that every geometric stalk of $\tau_E$ is an isomorphism in every cohomological degree. Step 2 exhibited $\tau_E$ as a morphism of bounded-below etale-origin objects. Apply precisely clause 3 of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] to this morphism: $\tau_E$ is an isomorphism. This invokes the etale-origin criterion, and makes no assertion that geometric points detect all pro-etale sheaves. Step 3 already proves its base-change compatibility.

source.place: Step 2, last sentence: global isomorphy from the correct conservativity statement

proof.text:
Define $\operatorname{tr}_\pi=\tau_E^{-1}$. Inverting the identity of Step 3 proves the same base-change compatibility for this trace. Finally [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] applies with $K=A_E$ and $L=A_B(1)$: both are bounded constructible and $L$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], with its prescribed pro-etale realization as in [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. It identifies
$$R\pi_!A_E(1)[2]\cong(R\pi_!A_E)\otimes_A^L A_B(1)[2].$$
Tensor with $A_B(-1)[-2]$. The evaluation and twist-pullback identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], realized with the same finite twist, cancel $A_B(1)$, giving $R\pi_!A_E\cong A_B(-1)[-2]$.

The dependency closure has no cycle (14,280 nodes); all cited ids exist and none is merged. The only near-duplicate is thm-pur-vector-bundle-thom, a rank-r generalization that cites this item, so same_as=[] is right. The proof follows the unit's route: affine-line integration through the P1 compactification and j_!. Fault, C3/C4, fixed: Step 1 identified the class cl of lem-pur-divisor-class with c_{z(B),A} of lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map by 'the same construction', but that construction is only in lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map's proof. Its stated properties do not pin the morphism down, since two such morphisms can differ by H^1(E-z(B),A(1)). I rewrote Step 1 to use statements only: lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map says its morphism is the realization of an etale morphism on a stated etale witness; lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer says that etale morphism is built from the same Kummer boundary and is the scalar extension of the Z/N version; def-pur-frame-class gives the same projection onto the twist. I added lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer and def-pur-frame-class to the step's uses, and def-pur-frame-class to proof_deps; the corrected file is at fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/thm-pur-rank-one-thom.json. Steps 2–9 check against the cited statements. Step 2: z is proper, Rz_! = z_*, the identity-normalized composition gives the source, and tau_E is the realization of an etale morphism. Step 3: the compact-support exchange from thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale; the source component is the identity by vertical pasting (thm-cbc-finite-torsion); valid for non-flat g. Step 4: the hypotheses of lem-pur-cfiber-stalk (D^b_ctf) and the comparison over K_0=Omega hold. Step 5: the hypotheses of the P1 decomposition hold; the restriction map is (1,0), since the h-component is zero because H^2(Omega,A(1))=0; the long exact sequence makes beta invertible. Step 6: the counit e is an isomorphism and the naturality square holds. Step 7: O(D_0)=O(1) with the convention e_0=t^{-1}e_1, so beta tau_X=1 and the normalization coefficient is +1. Step 8: clause 3 of the conservativity lemma (etale origin). Step 9: projection formula with L of Tor amplitude [0,0], then evaluation, giving A_B(-1)[-2]. Small cases checked: B empty, B a point, B non-reduced, n not divisible by the ramification index, non-flat base change, a non-trivial line bundle. I accept the six declared tool_uses as generic black boxes. No SGA source is cited.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
